group.title: Celebrations
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A special event or party for something good that happened.
examples: There was a big {celebration} after the team won.
wrong: The celebration was sad and nobody came.

words.meaning: To do something fun because it is a special day or good news.
examples: We {celebrated} her new job with dinner.
wrong: They celebrated the good news by sitting in silence alone.

words.meaning: Something you give to someone, for example on their birthday.
examples: Thank you for the lovely {gift}!
wrong: She paid me back for the gift I gave her.

words.meaning: A thing you give to someone on a special day.
examples: I got a book as a birthday {present}.
wrong: He bought himself a present and kept it in the shop.

words.meaning: A card or message asking someone to come to an event.
examples: I got an {invitation} to their wedding.
wrong: The invitation told me not to come.

words.meaning: The person who invites guests and looks after them at a party.
examples: The {host} gave everyone a drink at the door.
wrong: The host was a guest who came to the party late.

words.meaning: A stick of wax with a string in the middle that you burn for light.
examples: There were ten {candles} on the birthday cake.
wrong: She turned on the candle with a switch.

words.meaning: A small colored rubber bag that you fill with air.
examples: The children played with red {balloons} at the party.
wrong: The balloon was heavy, like a rock.

words.meaning: A pretty thing you put up to make a place look nice for a party.
examples: We put {decorations} on the walls for the party.
wrong: The decorations made the room look plain and empty.

words.meaning: A holiday on December 25 when many people give presents.
examples: We eat a big dinner with family at {Christmas}.
wrong: Christmas is in July every year.

words.meaning: The first day of January, when the calendar starts again.
examples: Happy {New Year}! Let’s hope this year is great.
wrong: We celebrate New Year in the middle of June.

words.meaning: October 31, when children dress up and ask for candy.
examples: My son was a ghost for {Halloween}.
wrong: Halloween is a summer holiday in August.

words.meaning: An American holiday in November when families eat a big meal together.
examples: We eat turkey at {Thanksgiving}.
wrong: Thanksgiving is a day when nobody eats.

words.meaning: When people lift their glasses and drink to wish someone well.
examples: Let’s make a {toast} to the happy couple!
wrong: He gave a toast by putting his glass down and leaving.

words.meaning: Something you say when you touch glasses before drinking.
examples: Everyone lifted their glasses and said, ’{Cheers}!’
wrong: He said cheers when he was angry and wanted to leave.

words.meaning: What you say to someone when they do something good.
examples: {Congratulations} on passing your driving test!
wrong: She said congratulations because he failed his exam.

words.meaning: A long thin piece of pretty cloth tied around a gift or in hair.
examples: The box was tied with a gold {ribbon}.
wrong: The ribbon was a thick, heavy piece of wood.

words.meaning: A folded card with a picture and a message for a special day.
examples: I wrote a short message in her {greeting card}.
wrong: He opened the door with a greeting card.

words.meaning: A woman or girl who helps the bride on her wedding day.
examples: My sister was a {bridesmaid} at her friend’s wedding.
wrong: The bridesmaid was the man getting married.

words.meaning: A very large, special meal for many people.
examples: The wedding {feast} had ten kinds of food.
wrong: The feast was one small cookie.

words.meaning: A party that is kept secret from the person it is for.
examples: We planned a {surprise party} for Mom’s fiftieth birthday.
wrong: We told her all about the surprise party a month before.

words.meaning: A formal event with special actions, like a wedding.
examples: The wedding {ceremony} was in a small church.
wrong: The ceremony was a quick chat in the kitchen.

words.meaning: A ring that a married person wears, often gold.
examples: He put the {wedding ring} on her finger.
wrong: She wore her wedding ring on her nose.

words.meaning: A card you give someone on the day they were born.
examples: Everyone in the office signed her {birthday card}.
wrong: He sent me a birthday card on the wrong person’s wedding.

words.meaning: Done in the same way for a very long time.
examples: We cook a {traditional} dish every New Year.
wrong: It is a traditional song, so nobody has heard it before.

words.meaning: To take the paper off a present.
examples: The kids couldn’t wait to {unwrap} their gifts.
wrong: She unwrapped the gift by putting more paper on it.

words.meaning: A bunch of flowers tied together as a gift.
examples: He gave her a {bouquet} of roses.
wrong: A bouquet is one dead leaf.

words.meaning: To plan a party and invite people to it.
examples: Let’s {throw a party} for his birthday.
wrong: They threw a party and invited nobody.

words.meaning: A big fire outside, often for a party.
examples: We sat around the {bonfire} and sang songs.
wrong: We lit a bonfire inside the small bedroom.

words.meaning: Saying numbers backward, like ten to zero, before a special moment.
examples: We did the {countdown} together just before midnight.
wrong: The countdown went from one up to twenty.

words.meaning: Small sweet foods made with sugar.
examples: The kids got lots of {candy} on Halloween.
wrong: Candy is very salty and good for your teeth.

words.meaning: Pretty paper you use to cover a present.
examples: I need {wrapping paper} for her gift.
wrong: He wrote a letter on the wrapping paper and posted it.

words.meaning: Tiny pieces of colored paper thrown at parties and weddings.
examples: They threw {confetti} over the bride and groom.
wrong: They threw confetti, big heavy stones, at the couple.

words.meaning: To hope silently for something, often when you blow out candles.
examples: Close your eyes and {make a wish}!
wrong: She made a wish by shouting it to everyone in the room.

words.meaning: To stop a flame by blowing air on it.
examples: She {blew out} all the candles on her cake.
wrong: He blew out the candles and they burned brighter.

words.meaning: What you say to someone on the day they were born.
examples: {Happy birthday}! How old are you today?
wrong: I said happy birthday to him at his wedding.

words.meaning: A male friend who helps the groom at his wedding.
examples: The {best man} gave a funny speech.
wrong: The best man was the person getting married.

words.meaning: To put on special or fancy clothes.
examples: We all {dressed up} for the wedding.
wrong: He dressed up for the party in his old pajamas.

words.meaning: A party outside where food is cooked over a fire.
examples: We’re having a {barbecue} in the garden on Saturday.
wrong: We had a barbecue in the cold kitchen with no food.

words.meaning: A day when most people do not go to work or school.
examples: The banks are closed because it’s a {public holiday}.
wrong: On the public holiday, everyone went to work as usual.
